traits.habitat_notes: Dry rocky outcrops and slopes in the east of South Africa and Eswatini (also Mozambique); in dense stands in the Albany thicket (spekboomveld) of the Eastern Cape and the Little Karoo; browsed by elephants and black rhinoceros.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form chosen from the plant's habit: a dense, much-branched succulent shrub with reddish-brown stems and crossing pairs of small fleshy round leaves.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species.

allometry.note: 2.5 m tall at 15 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a dense, much-branched succulent shrub with reddish-brown stems and crossing pairs of small fleshy round leaves.

traits.woodiness.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): soft-wooded shrub or small tree.

traits.life_span.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): a long-lived shrub or small tree (perennial).

traits.leaf_habit.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): an evergreen, much-branched shrub (immergrün); English Wikipedia says semi-evergreen, so semi as the lesser state.

traits.height_typical_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): 2 to over 4 m tall; English Wikipedia: usually 2.5-4.5 m.

traits.height_max_m.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): usually 2.5-4.5 m tall.

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: an open-grown plant spreads about as wide as it is tall or less; Wikipedia says it grows dense enough to cover itself and forms thicket, but gives no width.

traits.stem_diameter_max_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the smooth, reddish-brown trunk reaches up to 30 cm across.

traits.stem_posture.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): an upright shrub; the cultivar 'Prostrata' is the decumbent exception.

traits.stem_clump.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: a much-branched shrub (German Wikipedia: stark verzweigt) with a short trunk or a few stems from the base.

traits.crown_form.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: dense, much-branched, rounded shrub crown with limber, tapering branches (Wikipedia: more loosely branched than Crassula, with limber tapering branches).

traits.bark_texture.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the trunk is smooth (glatt); the genus account adds that the bark peels.

traits.bark_colour.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): trunk reddish-brown (rötlichbraun); sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.twig_colour.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): commonly has a reddish stem; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.spines.note: German Wikipedia, 'Didiereaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): Portulacarioideae are unarmed.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): small leaves crosswise opposite (kreuzgegenständig) on shoots 3-6 mm thick with internodes 2-3 cm.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves kreuzgegenständig, decussate.

traits.leaf_form.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): simple, somewhat fleshy, thickish leaf blades.

traits.leaf_division.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves simple (einfach).

traits.leaf_shape.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves obovate (verkehrt-eiförmig); English Wikipedia: small, round pads.

traits.leaf_apex.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves with a fine short point (feinstachelspitzig), mucronate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves entire (ganzrandig).

traits.leaf_hairs.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves hairless (kahl).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves 13-26 mm long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves 10-21 mm wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves sessile to short-stalked (sitzend bis kurz gestielt); the 2 mm upper bound is our estimate for 'short' on a 13-26 mm leaf.

traits.leaf_colour.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): leaves green (reddish stem, green leaves); sRGB by eye for the word, a mid succulent green.

traits.leaf_posture.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves held spreading from the stem in opposite pairs, as photographs of the plant generally show.

traits.stipules.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): stipules absent (Die Nebenblätter fehlen).

traits.sexual_system.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): plants bisexual or female, that is gynodioecious (citing Venter et al. 1993); female flowers have staminodes. The vocabulary has no gynodioecious state; polygamous stands for the female plants.

traits.inflorescence.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): terminal inflorescences of very many small flowers, stalked, in tufts of 1-10; the species account: stalked flowers in clusters at the branch tips. Read as a panicle of small clusters.

traits.flowering_position.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): flowers clustered at the branch ends (an den Zweigenden).

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: the genus account says 'very many' flowers per terminal inflorescence, in tufts of 1-10; 20-100 is our reading of that.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: German Wikipedia says the flowers are stalked; 2-5 mm on a 3 mm flower is our estimate.

traits.flower_size_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): small flowers reaching 3 mm across.

traits.flower_colour.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): flowers pink or white (rosa oder weiß); pink taken; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.perianth.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): two persistent, joined sepals (or bracts, by another reading) and five fleeting petals (or tepals).

traits.flower_merosity.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): five petals.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the two persistent, joined sepals are 0.5 mm long.

traits.petal_length_m.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the five fleeting petals are 1.5 mm long.

traits.stamens.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): 5 to 10 stamens.

traits.anther_colour.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): anthers red to purple (rote bis purpurfarbene Staubbeutel); sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.carpels.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the superior ovary is three-angled and one-chambered with three almost sessile stigma branches.

traits.ovary_position.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): ovary superior (oberständig).

traits.fruit_type.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): small, three-winged, one-seeded fruits that do not open (Flügelnüsse).

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: German Wikipedia says only 'small' three-winged fruits; 4-6 mm across the wings is our estimate for a 3 mm flower.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: dry, papery three-winged fruits, pale pinkish when ripe; no source read names a colour.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: German Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): the two sepals are persistent (beständig); the family account says they wrap the fruit.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: southern-hemisphere spring flowering (about September to November in the Eastern Cape) is our recollection of South African accounts; SANBI PlantZAfrica, which states it, was blocked.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: a month or two after flowering, about November to January; no source read gives it.

traits.light.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): an easy house plant for a sunny place; endures desert sun once established.

traits.moisture.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): drought-tolerant; favours drier rocky outcrops and slopes; most abundant in the dry southern Cape.

traits.soil_texture.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): favours drier rocky outcrops and slopes; adds organic matter to sandy soil.

traits.habitat_notes.note: English Wikipedia, 'Portulacaria afra' (read 2026-10-19, lower trust): widespread in the east of South Africa and Eswatini, on drier rocky outcrops; densest in the Albany thickets of the Eastern Cape and the Little Karoo; eaten by elephant and black rhinoceros. German Wikipedia adds Mozambique and KwaZulu-Natal.

traits.leaf_succulence.note: Wikipedia and Flora of Southern Africa as summarised there, Portulacaria afra (read 2026-10-19): leaves small round pads, somewhat fleshy and thick, succulent.

traits.leaf_cross_section.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: a round pad thick and fleshy, flat above and rounded beneath, as photographs show.
